haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices to the shadow store for comparison only.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: Charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window triggers automatic rollback, in both or new_only (reversible, before day 35).
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates and Finance sign-off reset; the rollout must pass through shadow again, with the 7-day count restarting at zero.
haiku-low.q6: After 35 days in new_only (day 35 onward), because the usage events the old engine skipped have expired and the log no longer covers them.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED how workers learn of the change. A duplicate charge from disagreeing workers is stopped by the idempotency key. In-flight invoice handling is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: The controller keeps its own durable record outside the flag, holding gate counters and sign-off. It rejects any skipped step or any move whose gate is unmet.
haiku-low.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window and, above 2%, starts an automatic rollback.
haiku-low.q10: Charges that fall due are queued, not dropped. They are actually made at handoff, by the old engine, after freeze, drain, reconcile and reprocess.
haiku-low.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing period), attached to every charge and checked against the ledger and payment provider, lets them refuse a repeat charge. Reconcile matches the ledger to the provider first.
haiku-low.q12: Charging stays frozen, so charges are delayed, not dropped or doubled. After retries it goes to rollback_stalled and pages on-call. On-call fixes the cause and resumes at the failed step; steps are safe to repeat.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store only, and never charges.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, with no charging, so it stays current.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person advances the flag. The rollout controller rejects the move if the gate is not met.
sonnet.q4: A charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window for the new engine. It triggers automatic rollback in `both` and in `new_only` days 0 to 34 (reversible). It does nothing in `shadow` or `old_only`, and in `new_only_final` there is no rollback.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must pass through `shadow` again. Gate counters and Finance sign-off are reset, and the 7-day count restarts at zero. Gate A must be met again, then Gate B.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in `new_only`. The day-35 clock starts when `billing_mode` becomes `new_only`. After that the usage events the old engine skipped have expired, because the log keeps events for 35 days.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED. The document says only that `billing_mode` is in the config service, and that workers keep the last known mode if it is unreachable. It does not say how workers learn of a change or what happens to an invoice being processed. It says the idempotency key stops a double charge if workers briefly disagree.
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED for where the evidence is kept. The controller keeps a durable record of gate counters and the Finance sign-off, which is marked as the author's assumption to confirm. The nightly comparison job produces the mismatch data. The rollout controller rejects any skipped step or any move whose gate is not met.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED. The document does not name the component that detects the condition. It says the condition is the new engine's charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window. When it is met, automatic rollback starts. The rollout controller runs rollback.
sonnet.q10: They are queued, not dropped, from the freeze step on. They are made in the hand-off step, when the old engine charges periods that are due and not already charged, including the queued ones.
sonnet.q11: Reconcile matches the ledger to the payment provider, so each (customer, billing period) is known as charged or not charged. At hand-off the old engine charges only periods that are due and not already charged. Every charge carries the idempotency key (customer, billing period), checked against the ledger and the payment provider, which refuse a repeat charge.
sonnet.q12: After retries fail, the rollback goes to `rollback_stalled` and on-call is paged. Charging stays frozen, so charges are delayed but never dropped or doubled. The on-call fixes the cause and the rollback resumes at the failed step. Each step is safe to repeat.
